about: Built by data/build_indexes.py from the thesis-pipeline outputs (CS 156 captions, bge-m3). Real indexes on a tiny corpus: use the shapes of the curves, not the absolute numbers. Latency = this Mac, one CPU thread, one query at a time, median of 15 runs.

corpus.chunk_rule: at most 1,600 characters, 200 overlap, never across a 5-minute window

matryoshka.note: recall@10 of the truncated, re-normalised vectors against the same model's full-length exact top 10

filter_sweep.about: k of 18 lectures kept, 5 random lecture subsets per k (seeded), 43 questions (40 pilot + 3 demo), HNSW M 16; recall@10 against exact search inside the filter

layout.method: PCA of the 1,024-d vectors, first two components (explains 7.3% of the variance); for drawing only

lexical.analyzer: lowercase, words of 2+ letters or digits, drop English stopwords (bm25s list), Snowball English stemmer

questions.question: Why is a bigger margin better for generalization?
questions.why: A natural question that shares its key words with the lecture (margin, bigger, better).

questions.question: What does KKT stand for?
questions.why: An exact acronym: one rare token carries the question, the textbook case for keyword search. See whether it wins.

questions.question: Why does leaving a wide empty gap between the two classes help the classifier on unseen data?
questions.why: Q1 said in other words: it shares almost no rare word with the answer, which suits a dense embedding.
